<description>
**Problem:** A kernel application whose log callback logs, or destroys a kernel object, hangs. The common way to hit this is a garbage-collected language binding: Python's garbage collector can run finalizers inside the callback, and a finalizer that destroys a chainstate manager flushes and logs (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34775#issuecomment-6278257737, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4030551866). The cause is that the kernel calls log callbacks while holding the logger's mutex, so any logging from inside a callback blocks on a mutex its own thread already holds. The problem is not new and has existed since logging callbacks were introduced in #30595.

**Solution:** This PR delivers log entries through `btcsignals::signal`, which calls callbacks without holding any lock, replacing the kernel's own callback list and custom dispatching mechanism.

The change is a usability improvement and a bugfix because with it applications no longer need to reason about deadlocks and blocking behavior from a mutex they can't see. However, they may need to be updated to deal with log callbacks that are no longer serialized and connection functions that no longer block. Compatibility details are in the commit message.

The main code change is in `src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp` (+42/-77) accompanied by header docs and new test_kernel cases, which hang without the fix. There is also a commit switching `btcsignals.h` to use `StdMutex` instead of `Mutex` so it is safe to use in logging callbacks.

This is an alternative to the last commit of #34775, which fixes the same deadlock but only after limiting the process to one logging connection, and still hangs if a callback destroys the connection.
</description>

<commits>
e5c00b4bad ci: Add -Wno-error=maybe-uninitialized to i686 and Alpine musl tasks

GCC 15 at -O1 reports a false -Wmaybe-uninitialized for a
std::optional<btck::Logger<...>> in test_kernel.cpp, in the destructor
of a logger that is always emplaced before use. Don't fail the build on
it, as the armhf task already does.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5.

a520119c3f btcsignals: Use StdMutex so a signal can deliver log entries

Locking a sync.h Mutex can log: with DEBUG_LOCKCONTENTION it logs lock
contention, and with DEBUG_LOCKORDER it logs lock order errors. A signal
that delivers kernel log entries, as the next commit adds, would then
lock its own mutex again on the same thread while delivering that entry,
and deadlock. Use a StdMutex, as Logger in logging.h does for the same
reason.

The mutex only guards the connection list and is never held while
callbacks run, so lock order checking adds little here.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5.

25eff90bfd kernel: Dispatch log callbacks with btcsignals so they run without the logger mutex

KernelLogger called log callbacks while holding its mutex, so a callback
that logged, or destroyed a kernel object that logs, deadlocked. A
garbage collector running finalizers inside a callback can trigger this
(https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34775#issuecomment-6278257737).

Deliver entries through a btcsignals::signal instead, which holds no lock
while callbacks run. The API is unchanged. Behavior changes:

- Callbacks can run on several threads at the same time, so they must be
  thread-safe.
- Callbacks may call kernel functions, including creating and destroying
  logging connections, their own included.
- Destroying a connection no longer waits for invocations already
  running on other threads. The user data is destroyed when the last one
  returns, as with other btcsignals users.

This is the follow-up suggested in
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4034240501.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5.
</commits>
